title: Runtime 1.21 Launch Brief (Draft) — Kernel Auto-Selection v2 + Rollout Plan
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Runtime 1.21 Launch Brief (Draft)
Primary feature: Kernel auto-selection v2 (gated)
Prepared by: Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien)
Audience: Runtime, SRE, Control Plane, Perf/Evals, Support, PM
Last updated: 2026-02-23

Slide 2 — Why this release / Executive summary
What’s shipping:
- Runtime 1.21 includes kernel auto-selection v2 behind feature gates (default OFF unless allowlisted).
- Expanded kernel selection signals: model family/arch, seq-length regime (prefill vs decode characteristics), GPU SKU.
- Explicit fallback hierarchy + denylist for known-bad kernel/SKU/driver combos.
- Telemetry + dashboards for selection decisions and p95/p99 deltas.
- Determinism/replay tests and policy integration for predictable behavior.

What success looks like:
- Lower p95/p99 latency + improved throughput stability on heterogeneous fleets (A100/H100/L40S).
- Zero correctness regressions; deterministic selection under identical inputs.
- Safe staged rollout with rapid rollback and per-model/per-region overrides.

Slide 3 — Scope: what’s in 1.21
Core runtime changes:
- v2 selector decision logic + interface updates (candidate generation, scoring/rules, fallback).
- Model-family classifier integration (architecture tags / variants).
- Seq-length bucketing + prefill/decode regime heuristics.
- GPU SKU-aware kernel registry + normalization (including variants/MIG where applicable).
- Guardrail: auto-disable v2 on known-unstable driver/CUDA combos.

Ops / safety:
- Feature gate plumbing (environment/region/model allowlist + denylist, hot reload).
- Oncall tooling: force kernel, dump selection trace, pin/override.
- Deterministic replay tests wired into CI.

Observability:
- Per-request selection telemetry events (sampled) + aggregated metrics.
- Rollout dashboards: selection distribution + latency deltas + error rate correlation.

Out of scope (explicitly NOT in 1.21):
- Learned selection model / ML-based scoring.
- Automatic cross-region failover policies driven by selection output (kept separate).
- Any default-on behavior across all hosted traffic.

Slide 4 — Kernel auto-selection v2: key highlights (talk track)
Problem statement (v1):
- v1 selection is insufficiently SKU-aware and under-reacts to long-context regimes.
- Tail latency spikes observed when long-context workloads are misclassified or when kernels behave differently across drivers.

v2 improvements:
- Feature signals: (1) model family/architecture (Llama/Mistral/Qwen/Gemma/variants), (2) seq bucket / regime hints, (3) GPU SKU.
- Decision rules are explicit + debuggable; telemetry captures “why” (features + candidate set).
- Fallback hierarchy prevents hard failures when a preferred kernel is missing/unstable.
- Determinism: selection depends only on declared inputs; replay tests guarantee identical selection.

Slide 5 — Config / gates (how we control blast radius)
Gate layers (evaluated in order):
1) Global gate: kernel_selection_v2.enabled (per env)
2) Driver/CUDA guardrail gate: kernel_selection_v2.blocked_driver_versions
3) GPU SKU allow/deny: kernel_selection_v2.gpu_sku_rules
4) Model allowlist/denylist: kernel_selection_v2.model_rules
5) Region/cluster policy: kernel_selection_v2.region_rules
6) Manual override: forced kernel / disable v2 via runtime flags (for debugging)

Default posture for GA:
- Enabled only for explicit allowlisted model families + GPU SKUs in hosted canary clusters.
- Dedicated/Private: opt-in only (customer readiness review required).

Slide 6 — Rollout plan (staged)
Phase 0 — Preflight (complete/ongoing):
- Merge behind gates + CI determinism tests
- Dashboards live + sampling policy validated
- Bench matrix coverage complete for key model families + seq distributions + SKUs

Phase 1 — Hosted canary (Week 1):
- 1 region, 1–2 canary clusters
- Allowlist: 1–2 model families, conservative seq buckets
- Monitor: selection distribution, p95/p99, errors, fallback rate

Phase 2 — Hosted expansion (Week 2):
- Add 1–2 regions; expand allowlist by model family
- Expand long-context coverage only after confirming no tail regression

Phase 3 — Dedicated pools (Weeks 2–3):
- Start with internal Redwood dedicated pools
- External Dedicated: case-by-case, with customer comms + rollback plan

Phase 4 — Private deployments:
- Shipping in runtime 1.21, but stays OFF by default
- Enablement requires customer hardware matrix confirmation + runbook handoff

Slide 7 — Canary criteria (go/no-go)
Minimum bar to expand canary:
- Correctness: no increase in invalid outputs attributable to kernel selection; no new determinism failures.
- Reliability: error rate not worse than baseline (no new GPU/kernel launch errors).
- Performance:
  - p95 latency: no regression > 2% on the canary bundle; target improvement 3–8% depending on workload.
  - p99 latency: no regression > 1% for long-context buckets; any spike triggers immediate review.
  - Throughput stability: reduced variance in mixed workloads (qualitative + perf-canary).
- Fallback rate: stays within expected envelope (no “fallback storm” that hides a performance regression).

Automated signals:
- SLO gating checks from slo-toolkit rollout gate.
- perf-canary scenarios comparing v1 vs v2 by SKU and seq bucket.

Slide 8 — Key risks + mitigations (engineering)
Risk 1: Long-context misclassification causes p99 spikes
- Mitigation: conservative thresholds; long-context buckets rolled out last; explicit tests + perf suite coverage.
- Action owner: Lena Fischer + Marcus Reed (perf validation), Yuki Sato (rules).

Risk 2: GPU SKU naming/normalization mismatch (cloud instance variants, MIG)
- Mitigation: SKU normalization table + telemetry field for raw SKU; denylist supports quick blocking.
- Action owner: Isabella Rossi + Grace Kim.

Risk 3: Driver/CUDA-specific instability
- Mitigation: guardrail auto-disables v2 for known-bad combos; targeted validation plan.
- Action owner: Hiro Tanaka + Noah Patel.

Risk 4: Selector overhead / telemetry overhead
- Mitigation: sampling; microbench for selector eval cost; cache decision where safe.
- Action owner: Omar El-Sayed + Logan Wright.

Slide 9 — Key risks + mitigations (operational)
Risk 5: Debuggability during customer escalation
- Mitigation: runbook + CLI flags to force kernel and dump selection; clear rollback authority.
- Action owner: Kira Thompson (runbook), Sean Gallagher (oncall readiness).

Risk 6: Dashboard/metric cardinality issues (false positives / alert noise)
- Mitigation: pre-launch query review; metric cardinality controls; SRE sign-off.
- Action owner: Allison Grant + Aisha Bello.

Risk 7: Non-deterministic behavior in mixed workloads
- Mitigation: determinism/replay tests; ensure scheduler hints are stable and explicitly logged.
- Action owner: Jordan Lee + Sofia Ivanova.

Slide 10 — Observability plan (what we will look at)
Dashboards (rollout):
- Kernel selection distribution by: model, model family, GPU SKU, seq bucket, region
- p50/p95/p99 latency deltas: v1 vs v2 (where both are present)
- Error rate and GPU kernel launch failures
- Fallback counts and “reason codes”
- Selector overhead: time-in-selector (sampled) + kernel-switch overhead microbench trend

Sampling policy (target):
- Full event detail sampled (low %) + aggregated counters always on.
- Emergency knob to temporarily increase sampling for triage (time-bound, with SRE approval).

Slide 11 — Rollback plan (time-to-mitigate)
Rollback goals:
- Disable v2 within minutes without redeploy.
- Scope rollback to the smallest surface (model/GPU/region) first.

Mechanisms:
- Control plane: flip kernel_selection_v2.enabled to OFF (global) or add deny rule.
- Per-model denylist: block a single model version or family.
- Per-SKU denylist: block for a specific GPU SKU.
- Runtime flag override for emergency debugging in a single cluster.

Validation steps after rollback:
- Confirm selection distribution returns to v1 baseline.
- Confirm p95/p99 recovery on impacted routes.
- Confirm error rate returns to baseline.

Authority:
- Rollback decision maker on canary window: Release Train Lead (Connor O’Brien) in consultation with SRE oncall (Sean Gallagher / delegate) and runtime owner (Yuki Sato / Hiro Tanaka).

Slide 12 — Customer impact / external messaging (draft)
Customer-visible changes (Hosted):
- No API changes.
- Expected improvement: lower tail latency and more stable throughput for supported models/SKUs.
- “Behind the scenes” optimization; performance may vary by model and workload.

Customer-visible changes (Dedicated/Private):
- Shipped in runtime 1.21; remains OFF by default.
- Enablement by request after confirming GPU SKUs + driver versions.
- Provides stronger knobs for pinning/overrides during incident response.

Language we should use:
- Emphasize safety: gated rollout, quick rollback, determinism guarantees.
- Avoid promising universal improvements; scope to supported coverage.

Slide 13 — Internal comms plan
Audiences:
- Eng runtime + kernels: final checklist and canary schedule
- SRE/oncall: runbook walkthrough, rollback knobs, alert expectations
- Support/CS: what to ask customers (GPU SKU, driver/CUDA, model, seq length), known workaround (disable v2 / pin kernel)
- Product: release notes blurb and risk framing

Touchpoints:
- #eng-releases: launch timing + go/no-go updates
- #eng-runtime: technical triage during canary
- #eng-sre: dashboard/alert monitoring + rollback recommendation

Slide 14 — Timeline / milestones (proposed)
- 2026-02-24: final preflight review (dashboards, gates, runbook)
- 2026-02-25: Hosted canary start (Region A)
- 2026-02-27: expand canary to Region B (if criteria met)
- 2026-03-03: hosted expansion + model allowlist widening
- 2026-03-06: dedicated internal pools canary
- 2026-03-10+: external Dedicated opt-in windows

Notes:
- Dates are placeholders pending GPU capacity + oncall coverage confirmation.

Slide 15 — Launch checklist (condensed)
Must have:
- Feature gate confirmed (default OFF; allowlists validated)
- Runbook reviewed by SRE + Runtime oncall
- Rollout dashboards live, correct, low cardinality
- perf-canary scenarios passing; benchmark matrix coverage signed off
- Determinism/replay tests passing in CI
- Known-issues list reviewed; denylist updated
- Support brief ready (FAQ + escalation template)

Nice to have:
- One-pager of SKU normalization mapping for Support
- “How to reproduce locally” snippet for kernel selection traces

Slide 16 — Open questions / asks
1) Final default allowlist for Hosted canary (models + SKUs) — owner: Yuki Sato / Hiro Tanaka
2) Sampling rate for detailed events — owner: Omar El-Sayed / Logan Wright / Allison Grant
3) Dedicated enablement policy: who signs off per customer? — owner: Lauren Bishop / Markus Klein
4) Any additional driver/CUDA combos to preemptively block? — owner: Grace Kim / Noah Patel

Slide 17 — Appendix: owners / points of contact
Release train: Connor O’Brien
Program management: Talia Benson
Runtime kernels lead: Hiro Tanaka
Selector logic: Yuki Sato
Perf/correctness guardrails: Noah Patel
Observability/tail latency: Omar El-Sayed
Control plane gates: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor / Jordan Lee
SRE: Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant / Aisha Bello
Perf suite: Marcus Reed / Claire Dubois
Docs/runbook: Kira Thompson / Elliot Price

Slide 18 — Appendix: quick troubleshooting crib notes
If p99 spikes on long-context:
- Check selection distribution shift (seq bucket) + fallback reason codes
- Disable v2 for that model family in affected region
- Consider pinning kernel to known-good for the SKU
- Collect selection trace + raw SKU + driver/CUDA versions

If errors increase (kernel launch failures):
- Check denylist coverage; block kernel/SKU/driver combo
- Roll back v2 globally if multi-SKU

If dashboard alerts look wrong:
- Validate metric cardinality; switch to aggregated counters
- Coordinate with SRE before increasing sampling
